title: Chapter 61: Affection Level Increase
html:
Chen Ge was thankful that he didn’t say anything bad about Zhang Ya earlier. He laughed awkwardly and said, “I came out for fresh air because the dance studio was a bit too stuffy.”

Blood ran down Zhang Ya’s uniform as she stared at Chen Ge. Then she raised one slender, pale arm and pointed toward the teachers’ lounge.

“You want me to go there?” Zhang Ya vanished before he received an answer. Only a few meters from the gate, Chen Ge faced a dilemma. Returning to investigate meant risking further danger; leaving now meant abandoning the truth when it was almost within reach.

Zhang Ya’s attitude toward me has softened. Her hint must relate to the case from four years ago. But this school contains other presences like her—more than one. I should wait for the police before going back inside.

After climbing out of the school, Chen Ge kept watch outside the gate. He did not know whether Zhang Peng was still alive and dared not relax. Fifteen minutes later, dazzling headlights cut through the darkness. Two police cars approached.

Chen Ge jumped out into the road and waved the flashlight on his phone. “I’m here!”

The cars stopped outside Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy. Inspector Lee emerged with an officer Chen Ge had never seen before.

“Uncle Lee, you got here quickly.” By Chen Ge’s calculations, the police should have needed another half hour.

“We received a distress call from a taxi driver earlier, saying he was getting robbed, so we were already on the way to this place.” Inspector Lee had heavy circles under his eyes, signs that he had overworked himself for the past few days.

“Is that so? Either way, hurry inside. Zhang Peng should still be in the school!” Chen Ge pointed through the abandoned gate like a host welcoming guests into his home.

“Da Yong.” At Inspector Lee’s call, a muscular officer nearly six and a half feet tall retrieved bolt cutters from the trunk. “Exercise extreme caution inside the grounds. The suspect is cunning, so remain in pairs.”

He turned to look at Chen Ge. “Where is the last place you saw the suspect?”

“At the dance studio, but he already fled. I have something else to show you.” Chen Ge joined Inspector Lee and pointed toward the teachers’ lounge. “Would you come with me?”

“Da Yong, watch the road. Everyone else, proceed as planned.” After issuing his orders, Inspector Lee followed Chen Ge into the teachers’ lounge.

The building stood only three stories tall, but its interior was far more refined than any other part of the school Chen Ge had seen.

Inspector Lee held the flashlight in his hand and asked, “Why are we here? Did you see the suspect run this way?”

His eyes sharpened, and all weariness fell away. The moment he entered a potential crime scene, Inspector Lee became another man.

“Zhang Peng wouldn’t have come here.” Chen Ge led the way, searching for the exact room Zhang Ya had indicated. “I’m taking you somewhere connected to that girl’s death four years ago.”

“Haven’t I said I will help you investigate that after we capture Zhang Peng? The two cases cannot be mixed together, and the most important thing now is to capture Zhang Peng.”

“Here. This is the room.” Chen Ge ignored the objection. He had waited for the police precisely to minimize the danger. A sign identified the room as the sports-equipment storeroom. They tore away the seals, kicked open the door, and entered.

Balls littered the floor, while tennis rackets, table-tennis paddles, and other equipment hung from the walls.

“You brought me here to see this?” Inspector Lee used his flashlight to scan the corners of the room. “What can it prove?”

“Sports equipment…” Chen Ge moved to the room’s center and began searching. Beside the innermost cabinet stood a narrow single bed, much like the custom-made one in the dance studio.

“Why would a storeroom need a bed?” Frowning, Chen Ge lifted the wooden slats and exposed a horrifying sight.

Ten women’s ballet shoes of varying sizes lay beneath the dusty frame. One pair had been stained black with blood.

“So many?” The deliberately concealed shoes left Chen Ge too stunned for anger. Whatever had happened at Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy was more horrifying than he had imagined.

“There’s more than one victim!” Chen Ge turned to Inspector Lee. “Why would the dead girl’s ballet shoes be hidden here? Did the case report mention them?”

“The report never mentions them.” Inspector Lee frowned. “They’re covered in dust, so they must have been here for years. Yet someone arranged them carefully in a row, as though preserving them… perhaps they were the killer’s trophies.”

“Uncle Lee, you’re the officer. You have to get justice for the victims.” Chen Ge set the boards aside. “The killer had unrestricted access to both the dance studio and this storeroom. He was probably a custodian or security guard.”

“If you’re right, that narrows the search considerably.” The blood-darkened dance shoes hardened Inspector Lee’s expression. “I won’t rest until we uncover the truth. Whoever the killer is, I’ll see him punished to the full extent of the law.”

At his words, Chen Ge’s black phone vibrated. He took it out and found a new message.

“Managed to locate Zhang Ya’s red dancing shoes before dawn. Completed Zhang Ya’s Bloody Heart Mission, Mission Completion Rate: 50 percent.

“Zhang Ya’s affection level toward you has increased! You can write something you want her to do in Zhang Ya’s personal profile page (Note: It mustn’t be against Zhang Ya’s will).”

Chen Ge quietly retreated toward the door. Tonight was harrowing, but at least something good came of it.

He opened Zhang Ya’s profile page, and the display immediately turned red. My request can’t go against Zhang Ya’s will. That’s the only restriction.

After some thought, Chen Ge wrote, “I hope Zhang Ya will listen to me forever.”

“I’m sorry, but your demand is against Zhang Ya’s will, please change it.”

“I hope Zhang Ya will protect me from being harmed.”

“I’m sorry, but your demand is against Zhang Ya’s will, please change it.”

“I hope Zhang Ya will not harm me or harbor any intention to kill me!”

That’s doable, right?

“I’m sorry, but your demand is against Zhang Ya’s will, please change it.”

Er…
